docs.title: Welcome
docs.text: The climex package downloads climate data of Mexico from the NASA POWER API: daily, monthly or climatological temperature, precipitation, humidity, wind and radiation for the 2,465 municipalities of Mexico (INEGI 2019), whose points come with the package, or for any set of points, such as the AGEB or localities of a city. It downloads one request per point with all the period, up to five at a time, retries when the API is busy, can be stopped and resumed, and returns one row per point and date, without duplicates.

docs.title: Philosophy
docs.text:
The authors' vision is to create data packages, functions, or a combination of both in Julia, R, and Python, contributing to the interoperability of algorithms and data to transform the information into decisions that help solve specific problems.

In the case of climex, the climate is one of the main drivers of the transmission of dengue and other vector-borne diseases: the package gives the climatic covariates (temperature, humidity, precipitation) at the level used by surveillance and early warning systems, the municipality, in a single call. It is part of the dengueverse, and its R version is climex.

docs.title: From GitHub
docs.text:
pip install git+https://github.com/fdzul/climex-py

The package is installed as climex-py and imported as climex.

docs.title: 1. Import the package
docs.text: import climex

docs.title: 2. Choose the points
docs.text:
The municipalities of a state, of several states or of all the country:

yuc = climex.municipalities("31")              # the 106 municipalities of Yucatán
mx = climex.municipalities()                   # the 2,465 of the country

docs.title: 3. Download the climate
docs.text:
clima = climex.download_nasa_power_data(
    yuc, id_col="CVEGEO",
    parameters=["T2M", "T2M_MAX", "T2M_MIN", "PRECTOTCORR", "RH2M"],
    start_date="20240101", end_date="20241231",
    temporal_resolution="daily", community="AG")

106 points; parameters: T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, PRECTOTCORR, RH2M; daily; community AG; 5 processes
106/106 points downloaded in … s
38,796 rows; 106 points; no duplicates
complete: 106/106 points with all the period

docs.title: 4. Use the data
docs.text:
clima[["identifier", "date", "T2M"]].head(3)
#   identifier       date    T2M
# 0      31001 2024-01-01  21.98
# 1      31001 2024-01-02  22.32
# 2      31001 2024-01-03  23.03

See the Quick Start for the details and the Examples for monthly data, the whole country, weekly updates and the AGEB of a city.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

• The package is now climex-py (repository fdzul/climex-py); it is still imported as climex. The name climex on PyPI belongs to another project.
  • Declared the dependencies (pandas, requests).
  • download_nasa_power_data(): monthly requests use the years of the period; missing values (-999) are NaN; the monthly table has year and month; processes=1 downloads in order; new argument verbose.
  • Downloads run in threads instead of processes: no if __name__ == "__main__" guard is needed in scripts (on macOS and Windows the processes failed without it).
  • Busy answers of NASA POWER (429, 5xx) are retried three times, and the points that still fail get a second round at the end.
  • The result has only the period requested, one row per point and date (no duplicates), sorted by point and date; at the end it reports whether every point has all the period and the days without data.
  • A point whose CSV in output_folder already has the period requested is not downloaded again (days not yet published, NaN, are asked again), so an interrupted download continues where it stopped; with a later end_date (an update) it is downloaded again (overwrite=True downloads everything again); repeated identifiers raise an error; the failed points are listed at the end.
  • New municipalities(): one point for each of the 2,465 municipalities of Mexico (INEGI 2019), bundled with the package, for all the country or by state; built with data-raw/municipalities.py.
  • New centroids(): a point inside each polygon (e.g. municipalities of rgeomex) ready for download_nasa_power_data().
  • spatial_resolution accepts only "point" (the regional API needs a bounding box, not a latitude and longitude); kept so the code of 0.1 runs.
  • The identifiers keep their leading zeros in the result (01001, not 1001).
  • load_centroid_data() keeps the municipalities of the state given by the first two digits of CVEGEO (before it compared the last three).
  • New build_url() and parse_response(); tests; documentation with mkdocs.
• First release of climex.

docs.title: Data source
docs.text: Please cite also NASA POWER: These data were obtained from the NASA Langley Research Center (LaRC) POWER Project funded through the NASA Earth Science/Applied Science Program. The municipalities are from INEGI (Marco Geoestadístico 2019).

docs.title: Municipalities
docs.text:
climex.municipalities() returns one point for each of the 2,465 municipalities of Mexico (INEGI 2019, Marco Geoestadístico), bundled with the package:

Column Description CVEGEO Municipality key (5 digits: state + municipality) CVE_ENT, state State key and name CVE_MUN, municipality Municipality key and name latitude, longitude Point used to download (WGS84) centroid_lat, centroid_lon Geometric centroid centroid_inside Whether the centroid falls inside the municipality area_km2 Area of the municipality 
climex.municipalities("31")                  # one state
climex.municipalities(["14", "31"])          # several states
climex.municipalities()                      # all the country
climex.municipalities("31", point="centroid")

By default latitude and longitude are a point that is always inside the municipality (its representative point). The geometric centroid falls outside 67 curved or fragmented municipalities, where NASA POWER would give the climate of a neighbour or of the sea; point="centroid" uses it anyway.

The table is built with data-raw/municipalities.py from the polygons of rgeomex.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Group Parameters Temperature (°C) T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, T2M_RANGE, T2MDEW, T2MWET, TS Precipitation (mm/day) PRECTOTCORR Humidity RH2M (%), QV2M (g/kg) Wind (m/s) WS2M, WS10M, WD2M, WD10M Radiation ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN, CLRSKY_SFC_SW_DWN, ALLSKY_SFC_LW_DWN Pressure (kPa) PS

The full list is in the NASA POWER parameter dictionary. community ("RE", "AG" or "SB") changes only the units of some parameters; "AG" (agroclimatology) gives precipitation in mm/day.

docs.title: Source
docs.text: NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources) gives daily data from 1981 for meteorology (MERRA-2 reanalysis) and from 1984 for solar radiation (CERES), on a grid of 0.5° × 0.625°.

docs.title: climex en español
docs.text:
Datos climáticos de México de la API de NASA POWER: temperatura, precipitación, humedad, viento y radiación diarios, mensuales o climatológicos para un conjunto de puntos, por ejemplo los centroides de los municipios, localidades o AGEB de rgeomex. Es la versión en Python del paquete de R climex, parte del dengueverse.

pip install git+https://github.com/fdzul/climex-py

Se instala como climex-py y se importa como climex.

import pandas as pd
import climex

pts = pd.DataFrame({"id": ["merida"], "latitude": [20.97], "longitude": [-89.62]})
clima = climex.download_nasa_power_data(pts, id_col="id",
                                        parameters=["T2M", "PRECTOTCORR"],
                                        start_date="20240101", end_date="20241231")

El paquete trae un punto por cada uno de los 2,465 municipios de México (INEGI 2019), para descargar el clima de un estado o de todo el país:

yuc = climex.municipalities("31")              # los 106 municipios de Yucatán
mx = climex.municipalities()                   # los 2,465 del país
clima = climex.download_nasa_power_data(yuc, id_col="CVEGEO",
                                        parameters=["T2M", "PRECTOTCORR"],
                                        start_date="20240101", end_date="20241231")

Por omisión el punto siempre cae dentro del municipio (punto representativo); con point="centroid" se usa el centroide geométrico, que cae fuera en 67 municipios.

temporal_resolution Filas "daily" una por día (date) "monthly" una por año y mes (year, month) "climatology" una por mes y la media anual (period)

Cada punto se guarda como <identificador>.csv en output_folder. La NASA pide como máximo 5 solicitudes simultáneas, por eso processes se limita a 5.

docs.title: climex – Examples
docs.text: This page provides practical examples of using climex to download and explore the climate of Mexico.

docs.title: Example 1: Daily climate of the municipalities of a state
docs.text:
import climex

yuc = climex.municipalities("31")
clima = climex.download_nasa_power_data(
    yuc, id_col="CVEGEO",
    parameters=["T2M", "T2M_MAX", "T2M_MIN", "PRECTOTCORR", "RH2M"],
    start_date="20240101", end_date="20241231", community="AG",
    output_folder="nasa_power_yucatan")

print(clima.shape)
print(clima.groupby("identifier")["T2M"].mean().sort_values().tail())

docs.title: Example 2: Monthly climate of all the country
docs.text:
mx = climex.municipalities()
mensual = climex.download_nasa_power_data(
    mx, id_col="CVEGEO",
    parameters=["T2M", "PRECTOTCORR", "RH2M"],
    start_date="20150101", end_date="20241231",
    temporal_resolution="monthly", community="AG",
    output_folder="nasa_power_mx_monthly")
mensual.to_parquet("clima_municipios_2015_2024.parquet")

docs.title: Example 3: Climatology (long-term average)
docs.text:
clim = climex.download_nasa_power_data(
    climex.municipalities("17"), id_col="CVEGEO",
    parameters=["T2M", "PRECTOTCORR"],
    temporal_resolution="climatology", output_folder="nasa_power_morelos_clim")
clim.pivot(index="identifier", columns="period", values="T2M")

docs.title: Example 4: Weekly update for an early warning system
docs.text:
The same call with a later end_date and the same output_folder only asks again what is new; the days not yet published come as NaN and are dropped.

from datetime import date, timedelta

end = (date.today() - timedelta(days=4)).strftime("%Y%m%d")
clima = climex.download_nasa_power_data(
    climex.municipalities(), id_col="CVEGEO",
    parameters=["T2M", "RH2M", "PRECTOTCORR"],
    start_date=f"{date.today().year}0101", end_date=end,
    community="AG", output_folder=f"climatic/year_{date.today().year}")
clima = clima.dropna(subset=["T2M", "RH2M", "PRECTOTCORR"], how="all")

docs.title: Example 5: The AGEB of a city (with rgeomex)
docs.text:
import rgeomex

ageb = rgeomex.extract_ageb(locality="Merida", cve_edo="31")["ageb"]
pts = climex.centroids(ageb, id_col="CVEGEO")         # a point inside each AGEB
clima = climex.download_nasa_power_data(
    pts, id_col="CVEGEO", parameters=["T2M", "PRECTOTCORR"],
    start_date="20240101", end_date="20241231", output_folder="nasa_power_merida")

docs.title: Example 6: Weekly series by municipality
docs.text:
clima["week"] = clima["date"].dt.to_period("W-SAT")
semanal = (clima.groupby(["identifier", "week"])
                .agg(T2M=("T2M", "mean"), PRECTOTCORR=("PRECTOTCORR", "sum"),
                     RH2M=("RH2M", "mean"))
                .reset_index())

docs.title: Example 7: Plot the temperature of a municipality
docs.text:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

m = clima[clima["identifier"] == "31050"]           # Mérida
ax = m.plot(x="date", y=["T2M_MIN", "T2M", "T2M_MAX"], figsize=(9, 3))
ax.set_ylabel("°C")
plt.show()

docs.title: Data licenses
docs.text: The climate data come from NASA POWER, which are free and open to everyone (NASA Earth Science data policy); please acknowledge NASA POWER when you use them. The municipalities are from INEGI (Marco Geoestadístico 2019), under the free use terms of INEGI.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide will help you install climex and download the climate of the municipalities of a state in a few minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Python 3.10 or higher. pandas and requests are installed automatically.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pip install git+https://github.com/fdzul/climex-py

docs.title: 1. Your first download
docs.text:
import climex

ags = climex.municipalities("01")            # the 11 municipalities of Aguascalientes
clima = climex.download_nasa_power_data(
    ags, id_col="CVEGEO",
    parameters=["T2M", "RH2M", "PRECTOTCORR"],
    start_date="20250101", end_date="20251231",
    community="AG", output_folder="nasa_power_ags")

docs.title: 2. What you get
docs.text:
• One row per municipality and day: identifier (the CVEGEO, with its leading zero), latitude, longitude, date and one column per parameter.
  • Only the period requested, without duplicates, sorted by municipality and date.
  • One CSV per municipality in output_folder (01001.csv, …).
  • A report at the end: rows, points, whether every point has all the period, and the days without data.

docs.title: 3. Temporal resolution
docs.text: temporal_resolution Rows Period "daily" one per day (date) start_date to end_date ("YYYYMMDD") "monthly" one per year and month (year, month) the years of start_date and end_date "climatology" one per month and the annual mean (period) long-term average

docs.title: 4. Stop, resume and update
docs.text:
Run it again

If the download stops (connection, many points), run the same call again: the points whose CSV in output_folder already has the period, with data in every day, are skipped. With a later end_date (a weekly update) the points are downloaded again; the CSV are replaced, never appended, so nothing is duplicated.

Days not yet published

NASA POWER publishes the last days with a delay of a few days. Those days come as NaN and are asked again in the next run.

docs.title: 5. Requests
docs.text: NASA asks for at most 5 simultaneous requests, so processes is limited to 5. Busy answers of the API (429, 5xx) are retried three times, and the points that still fail get a second round at the end. A request can have up to 20 parameters.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
Download NASA POWER climate data for the points of a table.

Each point is saved as a CSV in output_folder (<identifier>.csv). A point whose CSV already has all the period requested is not downloaded again (unless overwrite=True), so an interrupted download can be run again and continues where it stopped; if the period grows (e.g. an update with a later end_date), the point is downloaded again. Busy answers of the API (429, 5xx) are retried three times.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default df DataFrame

Points to download, e.g. the centroids of the municipalities or AGEB.

required lat_col str

Columns with the coordinates (decimal degrees, WGS84).

'latitude' lon_col str

Columns with the coordinates (decimal degrees, WGS84).

'latitude' start_date str

Period as "YYYYMMDD"; for "monthly" only the year is used.

'20150101' end_date str

Period as "YYYYMMDD"; for "monthly" only the year is used.

'20150101' parameters list of str

NASA POWER parameters. Temperature: T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, T2M_RANGE, T2MDEW, T2MWET, TS; precipitation: PRECTOTCORR; humidity: RH2M, QV2M; wind: WS2M, WS10M; radiation: ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN; pressure: PS.

('T2M', 'T2MDEW', 'T2MWET', 'TS', 'T2M_RANGE', 'T2M_MAX', 'T2M_MIN') temporal_resolution ('daily', 'monthly', 'climatology') "daily" spatial_resolution 'point'

Kept for compatibility with version 0.1; only "point" is valid (one request per latitude and longitude).

"point" community ('RE', 'AG', 'SB')

Renewable energy, agroclimatology or sustainable buildings (units).

"RE" processes int

Simultaneous requests (NASA asks for at most 5); 1 downloads in order. The requests run in threads, so no if __name__ == "__main__" guard is needed in scripts.

5 output_folder str

Folder for the CSV of each point.

'./nasa_power_data' start_col str

Columns with a different period for each point.

None end_col str

Columns with a different period for each point.

None id_col str

Column with the identifier of each point (else idx_<row>).

None return_consolidated bool

If True, return the data of all the points in one table; if False, the result of each download.

True overwrite bool

Download again every point, even if its CSV already has the period.

False verbose bool

Show the progress.

True

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

Columns identifier, latitude, longitude, the date (date; year and month; or period) and one column per parameter. Missing values (-999 in NASA POWER) are NaN.

Examples:

>>> import pandas as pd
>>> from climex import download_nasa_power_data
>>> pts = pd.DataFrame({"id": ["merida"], "latitude": [20.97], "longitude": [-89.62]})
>>> clima = download_nasa_power_data(pts, id_col="id", parameters=["T2M", "PRECTOTCORR"],
...                                  start_date="20240101", end_date="20241231")

docs.title: municipalities(cve_edo=None, point='inside')
docs.text:
One point per municipality of Mexico (INEGI 2019), all or by state.

The table comes with the package (2,465 municipalities), so no download is needed; it is ready for :func:climex.download_nasa_power_data with id_col="CVEGEO".

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default cve_edo (str, int or list)

State code(s) ("31", 31 or ["14", "31"]). None returns the 2,465 municipalities of the country.

None point ('inside', 'centroid')

"inside" (default) uses a point that is always inside the municipality (its representative point); "centroid" uses the geometric centroid, which falls outside 67 curved or fragmented municipalities (see the column centroid_inside).

"inside"

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

CVEGEO, CVE_ENT, state, CVE_MUN, municipality, latitude, longitude (WGS84), centroid_lat, centroid_lon, centroid_inside and area_km2.

Examples:

>>> import climex
>>> yuc = climex.municipalities("31")          # the 106 municipalities of Yucatán
>>> mx = climex.municipalities()               # all the country
>>> clima = climex.download_nasa_power_data(yuc, id_col="CVEGEO",
...                                         parameters=["T2M", "PRECTOTCORR"],
...                                         start_date="20240101", end_date="20241231")
